newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA JAN-NOV SALES RISE 25 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA JAN-NOV SALES RISE 25 PCT.

text.p: Czech Skoda Auto a.s., majority-owned by Volkswagen AG, said on Friday that its car sales for the January-November period hit 238,000, an increase of 25 percent over the previous year.
Skoda said in a statement that unit sales in the Czech Republic alone for the first 11 months of the year totalled 79,176, also an increase of about 25 percent.
It said that in November alone, total worldwide sales were 24,496 units, some 36 percent higher over the same period in 1995.
"The largest sales growth for November was in Sweden, where 756 cars were sold as opposed to 47 in November 1995," the statement said.

The statement added that Slovakia was the largest export market for Skoda, with 20,544 units sold to the end of November, followed by Germany (20,014), Great Britain (12,726), Poland (14,204), Austria (8,839), France (8,396), and Italy (8,198).
